_README: POETRY. The page at poetry.html renders this file and nothing else: its waiting
line while `poems` sits empty, and the spiral plus the 28-chapter grimoire once
verse arrives.
NOTHING REACHES THIS FILE BY HAND. Write it with, in the hub repo:
python scripts/poetry-curate.py --publish
Only would_publish: yes crosses, and poetry-curate.py -> PUBLIC decides which
fields travel. Never written_for, occasion, redactions_needed, notes or kind, and
never `context`: the raw context stays private in poetry-source/ forever.
`notes` here is NOT that context. It is the reviewed public note, written from the
context in third person with every claim about another living person's health,
sexual history, drinking or parenting removed, then signed off piece by piece by
the owner on 2026-11-02. It is tracked in the hub at projects/poetry/public-notes.json.
A piece carries: slug, title, text (line breaks verbatim), date (ISO), written,
written_precision, year, era, lines, length_band, season, age, theme, form, notes,
moods, image, and ci (its chapter's index in `chapters`).
`chapters` are the journal notes in date order. `pairs` are pieces that answer each
other. `facets` is a copy of projects/poetry/taxonomy.json. Edit the hub, not this.

poems.text:
When I gaze upon her visage now
I can't help but then wonder how

The vulgar words she crafts that be 
While the nobility of her spirit I see

Are like the storm that comes before 
the flowers bloom and shine once more 

Her delicate physique I think
mixed with the fiery spirit I seek
Is poison to my mind so weak

How Midas touch turns things to gold
So too this poison my thoughts I hold
Never-more will my heart be so cold 

I love you jade my heart and soul 
Please tell me not to be so bold

But I cant help the way I feel 
The things inside are no small deal 

I want to be the one for you
There isn't anything I won't do

For Slaying beasts or climbing heights
Are trivial when you're in my sights

My depths and limits know no bound 
When it comes to bringing your crown 

I want so bad to let these-thoughts out
So much indeed that I might just shout 

I LOVE YOU JADE AAAA@AAA@AAAAAAAAAAA
poems.title: Jade
notes: Possibly the first poem he wrote. He was not certain either.
For a girl named Jade. Never shown to her.
The fragment "Read as trochees" was meant to sit above it as a reading instruction. Whether the cadence landed is still open.

poems.text:
Walking through a forest where the leaves never stop falling 
Where the sky is always cloudy, thunder threatening to unleash a torrential downpour
The woodland creatures have all fled, taken shelter, gone silent 
Now no one remains except you, marching on towards the distant future 

Does the choice to continue down this path even matter? 
The leaves never stop falling
The sky never changes
The creatures will never return 

For some time he pondered motionlessly
A tree to the side of the path noticed 
Slowly, steadily, extending a slender root out to him
Grasping one of his rough boots, but this did little to break his thought
So struck by compassion, the tree began to shake and rustle its branches 
The pain of losing the branches was great
Unbearable had it not been to free the traveler from his mental labyrinth
A ray of light broke through the clouds
Piercing through the newly made cracks in the canopy  
Gently grazing his worn, tired cheeks
Respite in this moment, something he had not felt 
The root he noticed, the broken branches he saw
Then the tree, pointing up directly towards the sunlight
So grateful he was to this gentle tree, he picked one of its seeds and placed it in his bag
The light, now gone, lives only in his mind 
With the will to continue, to move on forward, to honor this tree, that fills his heart
No more stopping, no more wasted time
Go, be, the path stretches on 
Its time to move, its time to dance 
The traveler stepped forward again and again, never ceasing his rhythm until he would reach his end
poems.title: (Second; Unnamed)
notes: An argument with himself about whether to keep writing poems for women.
He proposed "The Woodland Wanderer" as a title, then left it unnamed.
He kept writing them for another five years.

poems.text:
Like the tide descends on the shoreline
An angel appeared to me today
Washing away the sand on the beach 
So too this angel swept away my mind

To try to put it into words would be an affront to her grace 
For she truly is an angel
Her full beauty only explainable by the Lord's divine blessing
But being the fool I am, I shall try to capture a fraction of my feelings with these words to come 

Her smile, so bright, will set gossamer cloth aflame 
Her eyes, so soothing, will calm a rampaging beast
Her voice, so delicate, will lullaby you into a trance 
Her gestures, so graceful, will entertain better than any ballet

Just the sight of this angel brings respite to the eyes
For beholding such a heavenly being is something your heart will never forget 
A blessing, she is, to all that she meets
Flowers bloom in the wake of her footsteps 
The rain stops falling, the sky clears up
The sun shines when she comes into view 
Time stops at the sound of her voice 
Miracles begin to happen at the thought of her
I truly am blessed to have witnessed the Lord's divine gift to the world
poems.title: Pt1.
notes: A friend had told him to write things down to get them out of his head. This is what came out.
For a girl he barely spoke to. Written across a day and a night.
He was twenty.

poems.text:
Like the sun surely rises each morn
My heart fills with energy at the prospect of a new day 

Time has swept away the past, and thrust the present upon ourselves 
Each passing moment, time relentlessly casts this curse upon all
A curse, it appears, to those living in the past 
A blessing, however, to those alive in the now
A harbinger of the end, to the minds of the future

Each second, gone, replaced by the next 
So fear not the regrets of the past 
So flee not to the uncertainty of the future
So find peace in the present 

Amidst the tides of life, the waves never stop churning 
Seek not to stop the motion, clinging on to the past 
Struggle not against the current, fighting for a future not meant to be 
Love the Ocean of life and trust in her waves
Let her carry you to the highest crests and the lowest troughs 

One day, the Ocean of life tossed me into a storm.
Strong winds changing directions rapidly, temperature freezing cold to burning hot, the waves battered by lightning
My fear of approaching the storm was great
The longer I hesitated, the strong the wind, hotter my surroundings, the more thunderous the strikes
Until I finally gave in to her might and let the Ocean guide me towards the spiral of chaos
My ears ringing, my skin began to sting from the heat, my mind filled with the terror of death
The end was in sight 
But not so fast
The Ocean takes and gives in mysterious ways 
For when we reached the heart of the storm
The winds ceased 
The air felt cool 
The clouds funneled outwards and the sky opened up 
An island appeared in the center of the storm 
A treasure chest upon this sandy shore 
Radiating a sense of familiarity and comfort, I approached the decorative box 
The key, she told me, was alive inside me
And the box revealed its contents at my touch 
Love 
Love, guarded by the most viscous tempest 
Love, only reachable within the moment
Love, the freedom to truly be alive 
A gift from the Ocean, a gift to change my life

So I resolved to continue this journey
Where the storm goes, I go
Because the center of the storm is where I belong 
In love, in peace, with my treasure. 
With you.
poems.title: Pt2.
notes: A continuation. They had mutual friends and little else.
He showed her both parts eventually. She found them endearing. He never established whether she knew they were about her.
They walked an empty campus together once, COVID tapering off. She mentioned she was single. He did not take the hint.
She was, by his account, the most striking woman he had seen in person, and that did a fair amount of the writing.
He calls it self-sabotage now: he spent the day fantasising about it instead of seizing it.

poems.text:
The Raven soars into the night sky
Rising above the tormented soil
Her guiding light a faint moon's glimmer
Like a silver bullet piercing the crisp air

Approaching her final destination, Solitude
A golden cage once, now stained black
Desecrated by the penumbra of hate 
A flower wilts in the distance

The Raven beats her cold wings melodically
Emitting a discordant harmony 
Evoking in all a deep primal fear

Frostbitten by a single glance 
Petrified by her lonely eyes 
Time stops dead at her approach 

A promise forgotten, a breach of trust 
No end in sight, her torture draws on

Her sorrows ignored, an apathetic crowd
Head held high, but drowning within 

If only they knew, if only they could see

Silence in Raven's tears, deafness in the air

Pt 2. The Raven's Rebirth 

Her frozen tears paint the sky crystal blue
Raven, a crashing comet, death descending
From this end, new beginning surging out

Wrapped into Fervor's zealous embrace
poems.title: About the girl with lonely eyes - The Raven
notes: He worked at a gym that summer and spent it writing about the people he watched.
This one for a woman on the stair stepper who looked thoroughly unhappy. The feeling was closer to recognition than to attraction.
Part two never got written.

poems.text:
Slinking around the verdant underbrush 
Donning a prideful smile, she prowls about
Gaze locked on target, prey frozen stiff

Life and Death standing near Action's table
The Tigress desiring her guest's company
Sinking in her ravenous bite, an invitation

To dine with Death, walking on with Life 
Perched at the summit, alone with her prize
Isolated by her grandiose semblance 

Ferocity rivaled solely by ambition 
Cloaked with insurmountable determination 
Obtrusive appearance veiling elegance

Resting behind her fearsome fangs, 
A blessed being perceives the world 

Underneath her battle-scarred skin, 
A curious creature caresses the land 

Beyond her proud sauntering, 
A sagacious spirit begets immeasurable grace

Peering through the eyes of the many 
Unable to see past the surface skin-deep
I wonder if I am the only one 
Who caught sight of the Tigress true nature
poems.title: The Tigress
notes: For Jocelyn, a bodybuilder. He wrote it out by hand and gave it to her on a first date, at a park.
She liked it. They dated through the summer, until he went back to school.
She had, in his description, the spirit of a tigress.
See The Tiger, written after it ended.

image.caption: July 2021. He worked at the gym; she trained there.

poems.text:
Adrift a tropical gyre 
Life's swift current sweeping onward
Rising and falling, the tides in motion

Upon a time the water's fervor waned
A glimpse into the deep I glanced
Shrouded in gloom, the ocean empty

Then suddenly, stirring all to life
A sweeping sensation, a warm embrace
Fears fading, hope conquering despair

The glimmering pearl sparkling gently
A soft radiance illuminating my gaze
Repose winning over the mind 

Surface smooth as fine gossamer silk 
Polished to precious perfection 
The flawless, finest jewel 

The flow forging a fine melody
A song soothing to spirit and soul
It calls to me as a choir of angels

Captivating, inspiring, awestruck 
A newfound spirit rising out
Motivation amplified by the heart of the pearl

Within my reach, center to my view
So far away, but so close to admire
Courage to claim this natural wonder

I must act, now or never
poems.title: The pearl
notes: A carpe diem poem, shown to a woman at the gym.
She liked it. Nothing came of it.
His retrospective note: at twenty, six foot, and in the best shape of his life, this read as endearing rather than alarming.

poems.text:
I HATE how they look 
I hate HOW they look 
I hate how THEY look 
I hate how they LOOK 

Creeping creatures surrounding my sight
Malice filling minds, weapons closed in hand

Pestilence piercing peacefulness
Despair devouring delight
Sickness scourging sanity

When will it end? 

Suffering taking hold of all my senses
Feelings fade to numbness 
Any pleasure repressed from perception 
Other emotions repossessed by pain 
Retreat unavailable, punishment unavoidable

When will it end? 

Plunging the knife, she scoffs ecstatically
Smirking at the crimson staining her nails
Enjoying each and every torturous moment 
Twisting the blade, savoring the finale
I hate the way this feels 

When will it end? 

She looks disappointed
Was I not enough? 
She speaks dispassionately
Can't you see I'm trying? 
She withdraws nauseated

When will it end? 

Her boundless spite, her infinite agony
10,000 judgments that I never spoke
Time after time, dawn drawing near
A pain in my heart as we drift apart
Little did I even know you

This must be the end
poems.title: The Plague
notes: Written while sitting with his own fear of rejection.
Addressed less to a person than to a type: the unobtainable woman.
I Love the Way They Look is its deliberate mirror.

poems.text:
To answer your question, this is for you
And the Plague, regretfully about you too

Stop reading this now if you do not care
About the daft whims of a humiliated fool
Else bear with me as I try to make amends
With my scattered, misguided emotions 

Lifting the veil of doubt, I will try to see
The way it plainly presents itself to me
Without painful prejudice, ill will cast away
To express what lies buried below my decay 

A need, a want, a desire for what? 
For attention? Or power? How about lust?
What do I seek? Where is it found? 
Why don't I finally answer this all now. 

Inside your smile, your laugh, your smirk
I lose my sense of passing time at work
Filling my eyes with soft, pleasant sights
Embracing my heart with homebound lights
A high like none other, when I'm close by you
I wonder, if perhaps, you feel this way too

Yet I struggle to act, thoughts freezing over
I clench my teeth, I look away for cover
No, these feelings aren't sane
They aren't meant for my brain 
I try with all my might
To put up a good fight 
But they just won't get out of my sight 

Alas the only thing left to do 
Is writing this silly love poem for you 
So shall I begin with some words of praise 
To help with navigating this messy maze 

Your hair like you figure, so sleek and slender 
Cascading behind, showing your splendor

Your voice a fine tune, soothing my ears 
Putting to rest my darkest of fears 

Your words honest with a sense of candor
Making you seem all the more grander 

A playfulness of spirit, a heart made of gold 
Your glory, your grace, my duty to extoll
The virtue you possess over beauty divine
Snatching my heart away, it must be a sign


Looking forward to seeing
poems.title: The Answer-
notes: Written immediately after The Plague.
About a coworker he wanted to ask out and never did.
Unfinished. He suggests cutting the last line and publishing it anyway.

poems.text:
Erupting from the mountain top 
Drifting down without any stop 
He yanks himself from Death's swift grip
Surviving the gauntlet, resuming his trip

Scarred and wounded, his body in tatters
Determination in heart, that's all that matters
Willpower strong, he embarks on a mission 
Chasing the wind, setting off with ambition

Until he encounters a formidable foe 
One whose purpose is disseminating Woe
Unsheathing the sword, he draws his Hope
Approaching the giant, target in scope 

Clashing their blades, slipping his slashes
Blood smeared vision, both covered in lashes
poems.title: The Trailblazer
notes: For a friend from the gym who kept him motivated.
An attempt to branch out — a poem about a man doing something impressive, rather than another one about a woman.
Intended as an epic. Abandoned early.

poems.text:
Afloat the ocean 

Sometimes
Soft waves dredging foam up to the shore
Other times
Rough waves crashing debris onto the beach 

Always 
A trove of treasures radiating brightly
Dazzling the countless onlookers 

Unreachable, unobtainable, unworthy
Sailors pass by in awe
This paradise seemingly out of reach
Filling their heads with "what ifs" 
Filling their hearts with unrealistic hopes

The lonely island carries on 
Desperate for another's empathy

If only they could understand the island's language 
If only they could see past the blinding treasure
poems.title: A distant isle
notes: Written watching the gym floor fill with people he would never know.
He describes feeling like an island.

poems.text:
A treasure, and a place, 
Meet at Time's rendezvous 
When Fate's cold embrace 
Slowly melted through 

And revealing a prize 
That lay deeply within 
Once sheltered from eyes 
Brought out by a grin 

With a large risky leap
Jumping into the unknown 
Waking up from a sleep
Climbing onto the throne 

The world in his hand
Filling out to his palm 
Shadows crumbling to sand
Turn uncertainty to calm 

A change in perspective 
Brought on by desire 
No longer defective 
A heart lit on fire 

Unfettered new wings 
Rising up to the sky 
To the place of kings
Locked on with both eye

A castle so grand 
Afloat on the clouds
Cascading the land 
Drawing great crowds

And Life's gracious gift 
Extending out with care 
Onto his finger swift
A bright gold light flare

The ring now he bears
Gilded by finest gold
With ample joy he shares
The mirror to his soul
poems.title: The ring
notes: A coworker's graduation ring went missing. Gold, and recovered in a spot too specific to be an accident.
The staff reviewed the cameras. It became an incident.
Not about a woman, which makes it unusual here.

poems.text:
Water trickling through the stream steady
Water guiding me till I'm finally ready 
An abundance of stones fill out my sight
The decision mine, to choose which is right

Plunging down my hand into the frigid flow 
I pluck up a stone from the waters below
Grabbing my attention, but only for a minute
I drop the stone back, and quickly forget it 

On and on, the cycle continued
Round and round, this process renewed
Stone after stone, all seeming the same 
"Wait just a minute!" I suddenly exclaim

Gently filling my hand, a stone there lies 
Shining, shimmering, captivating my eyes
Enthralled, entranced by this natural beauty
I must make it mine, it will be my duty

Held up to the sun, making light amplified 
Held close to my heart, bringing love inside
A gem, a stone, taken up into my life
A story, a beginning, with fulfillment rife

Continuing on, trekking further downstream
I can't help but fear this be but a dream
Pinching my skin, feeling the pain 
Nope, I'm alive, still here and sane 

Water changing color at my footsteps below
My heart beating boldy, beginning to grow
Never feeling before, a sensation so happy
Never getting before, what I needed so badly

Other stones lay around, but not do I care
The gem and my heart, a perfect pair
My gem, a gift, sent from the Divine
My gem, a hope, all a part His Grand Design
poems.title: My Gem
notes: On the prospect of a relationship that might actually work.
Written after a few good dates with Jocelyn.

poems.text:
I LOVE the way they look
I love the WAY they look
I love the way THEY look
I love the way they LOOK

Those two, right over there, a couple standing side by side
With just glimpse at their visages, took hold of the bystander's eye
Never having viewed before, such a pleasant pair of smiles
Their dazzling aura, its radiance seemingly extending out for miles

The couple, their eyes, are locked onto each other 
Though a minute goes by, they continue for another 
Until suddenly breaking his gaze, he lets out a lively laugh 
She too, in turn, reciprocates a gentle giggle to this gaffe 

Continuing on together, their stroll down the boardwalk
Mouths moving in pattern, engaged in a pleasant talk
Honesty in heart, expressed by their pure nature
Joy into the world, delivered by their pristine picture

Having reached the date's end, and just slightly still in sight
Coming closely together, tightly hugging with all their might
Their date a success, filling onlookers with glee 
He leans in for a kiss, bashfully returning it does she 

Seeing two spirits aflame, brought together by fate 
Hoping that someday, the bystander might be able to relate 
Like a wick catching spark, their lives feel a bit brighter
The day marching on, their hopes raised a bit higher 

Though just a fleeting moment, it runs around in their mind 
Wishing and wondering, perhaps something similar they might find 
Picturing the couple again, so sweet, so simple, so real 
Feeling the warmth shared, in their hearts the couple an ideal
poems.title: I love the way they look
notes: The mirror of The Plague. Same subject, opposite weather.
About a couple who appeared to have it sorted.

poems.text:
Closing my eyes and hoping to see 
A guardian, an angel protecting me 
Opening my eyes and feeling nearby 
The gentle fluttering of an avian ally

The Hummingbird sent from Heaven on high
Wiping away a tear from my eye 
The sorrow, the pain, any tragic event
All blown away by this bird's movement 

I can't help but wonder if this is a sign
When I needed it most, becoming mine
Calming my nerves and embracing my heart
Negative feelings starting their depart 

Oh Hummingbird, how are you here today
Working your wonders in a mysterious way
Sent by someone watching above 
Filling me with comfort, safety, and love 

I know you must go, but we'll meet again 
Sooner or later, when things come to end 
We'll be there together, side by side 
With hand in hand, walking stride by stride 

Until that day comes, I'll try to be strong 
I'll look out for you, keep singing your song
poems.title: The Hummingbird from Heaven
notes: For Jocelyn, who had a hummingbird tattooed on the back of her neck.
She read the bird as protection. It had turned up at several decisive moments in her life.
He notes, from a distance, that a tattoo was an unusual conclusion for a devout Christian to reach.

poems.text:
The warmth of a thousand blazing bonfires 
The cheerfulness of a rich holiday feast 
Our hearts mimicking the tide's rhythm swift
A safehouse securely soothing my skin 

Holding in my mind, sweet images of you
Holding in my hand, your palms so cute
Delicate and fragile, but firm and strong
Calloused knuckles, shifting smoothly along

Time drifting away without anyone's notice 
Your loving touches conjuring a blissful lul
Each second adding depth to my happiness
Until, like your affection, its limit boundless

Her patience envied by saints most pious
poems.title: Within your arms
notes: About being touched.
She was his first girlfriend, at twenty. He describes himself as touch-starved before her.

poems.text:
Open your eyes.

His golden locks flailed in front of his eyes, partially obscuring his vision. Losing his footing as the sweat trickled down his face, he steadied himself. Death chasing closer, nipping at his heels. The sound of fetters clinking and clanking together pounded in his eardrums louder, louder. Fear striking at his heart telling it to beat faster, faster. 

Driving himself down the mountain, he mustered all the power in his worn down body. His lungs burning hotter than ever before, he panted hard as he was running out of breath. Breaching the hazy horizon, and with a breath of fresh air, the oasis grabbed hold of his gaze. With safety just barely in sight, the finish line seemed so close. Finally his hardships are coming to a close. 

But the feeling of relief was short-lived. Reaching out from the freezing fog behind, the cold hand of Death grabbed hold of his ankle. Memories of the time he spent with Death crept up from a place long forgotten. A wave of calm fell over his soul. Death showing him a life of comfort, a life of pleasure, a life of the past. A life he used to have in a time not so long ago. 

With a chuckle and a grin, Death lured Carson in. "See, isn't this so nice?" Asked Death with a cackle. And opening a manacle, Carson slowly reached over. Placing his left hand in first, he gave in to Death's pleasing lure. "I knew you'd come back. You belong with me here, in the time of our past." Death said, letting out a hysterical laugh. Sweeter than peach nectar and smooth as silk, Death charming him in with his promising words. 

As his right hand resigned into Death's trick, a sudden thought graced his mind. 

Is this what I want? A life without suffering, just giving into ease? He thought as his mind began to wade into Death's lull.

 No, this doesn't have to be it. It's not my time yet. Carson awakening from his hypnosis
poems.title: For Carson
notes: For a man at the gym who lifted with more ego than judgement.
The conceit: a race to the grave, Carson against Death.
Never finished. Carson thought it was lame.

poems.text:
The sunlight fell upon the cracked soil 
As a sweltering heat stirred the stiff air
How long must the weary laborer toil 
How long must we wage war against despair 

Because on that day when the end felt near 
No man could predict what would come next
They held their actions and waited in fear 
Praying their futures would not be hexed 

So on that day when trees held their breath 
The Earth trembled at the powerful hands
And the spirits swirled away from death 
Erupting in unison and coloring the lands

And on that day when the world stood still
No creature dared shatter the freezing silence 
For the time had come to fulfill His will
And to do so graciously, without violence

Finally an end, or a beginning new truth 
Blessed by Fortune and embraced by Love
Molting new wings forged from youth
Flowing pure life, emulating the Dove
poems.title: The Day Time Stopped
notes: The same day, from closer in.
He had a few weeks left on the schedule and used them to keep writing.

poems.text:
The Tiger hidden inside me 
Is the one thing I must be 
Stronger than ever before 
A power that I cannot ignore 

Surging up without a doubt 
Letting out a screaming shout 
As the Raven's talons pierce skin 
My hate, my rage, my pain flows in 

But swallowing up the hopeless despair 
In my heart, a faint, soft voice there 
Remember what it is that I saw 
That tender, loving spirit of awe 

And ripping out the talons deep 
Despite my agony, I took the leap 
To find that piece always missing 
That peace, called joy, always wishing

No matter the cost, or high the price 
I resolve to rid myself of vice 
Living out the way of the Tigress 
Survival no longer feeling lifeless 

She showed me how I should be 
Blazing a new trail, setting me free 
Pursuing the path to such new heights 
Searching, hunting, chasing those sights

But at the Tiger's center remaining steady 
Holding her words always at the ready 
To become your truest, happiest self 
I'll be praying for you, without a doubt
poems.title: The Tiger
notes: The companion piece to The Tigress, written after it ended.
She gave his things back one Friday after his shift. They made protein ice cream, watched the sunset out of the back of her car, and swapped belongings in the parking lot.
See also The Day Time Stopped.

poems.text:
A note placed upon our door
I wonder what it might be for
Meaning of the message murky
Although the quote quite quirky
Its purpose I wish to know more
And the heart at the bottom I cannot ignore
Lest this be a sly ruse
This poem, I beg, you do excuse
poems.title: The Note
notes: Written after he moved back onto campus for his sophomore year.
The neighbours left a note on the door, suggestive enough to merit a reply.
It came from a room of four women. He replied in verse.
It went nowhere.

poems.text:
To be the me I was with you
To keep the flame alive 
To see the world with that same view
To take it in and thrive 

To be the me I was with you
To hold that courage in my hand
To make the step into a new
To harvest the fruits of the land

The me I was within your eye
The picture-perfect scene
The power I felt flowing inside
The love that is unseen

The me I am within your mind
The me I’m meant to be
The me, right now, that you will find
The me that conquered me

A me that exists because of you
A dream rooted into reality
A me that became one of the few
A grasp firm onto causality 

A fine future falling into place
A set of wings starting to sprout
A goddess as my guiding grace
A destiny my desire to carry out
poems.title: The me I was with you
notes: An inventory of who he had been while it lasted.

poems.text:
The stage was decorated extravagantly with emptiness
As time creeps forward ever so slowly, the clock strikes midnight 
Hush now, as silence descended to drown out the lonely spectators
The play, with no protagonist, is about to begin
The play, without an audience, never reached its end
 
How dreary the lives of the useless antagonists
How weary the minds of the slothful, dampened spirits
These nameless words falling into a forsaken mind
These nameless verses working to change something in kind

What does it take to restore sight to the blind?
What does it take to show love to the maligned?

Whatever the heart holds closest as it desires
Is found in the flowing dance of fervent fires
And to enter the song is as simple as this
Grab hold of their hands exuding such vis

Step by step, waltzing back into the light
The play truly beginning now, the stage blazing bright
Forgetting what’s been done to restrain your vivacity 
Rejoicing for it’s the time to restore your voracity

I want you to know a great secret of mine
My secret I’ll share, a gift from the Divine
That Heaven is only found once you’ve been through enough Hell
There lies joy, so boundless, such I cannot even begin to spell

Though the highway to Heaven is paved by pain
The journey, the suffering, the dance done not in vain 
Because for you there exists such a beautiful domain
It’s been patiently waiting all along for you to attain

Should these words not suffice
The nameless poem I’ll write twice
I simply want you to see
The truth you can be

So even if the future may seem remote
Please, please, don’t give up your hope
And try not to let your audience down 
Put on your best smile, do away with that frown

Dance my dance, I’ll even teach it to you
Try it for once, it might change your view
For life’s silliest challenges are faced by the funniest clowns 
Come enroll in the circus and you’ll never be let down
poems.title: Without title
notes: For Anna, who played in e-sports. He showed it to her once.
She did not understand it. They went on something adjacent to a date.
She folded him paper cranes. They are still on his monitor.

image.caption: The cranes she folded. Still on his monitor.

poems.text:
On my trek toward the festival in glee 
I happened upon quite a sight to see
A dazzling light shone out through the dark 
My curiosity ignited as quick as a spark

A soft, pale emerald gaze fell upon me 
And following so a figure of divinity
The trees clamored about in her wake 
Nature dancing and applauding for her sake

Twisting about our paths with fate 
Generous gods granting gifts so great
A delightful presence and sagacious grace
Her aura so pure and how sweet her face

For the visage I saw and began to adore
Dotted with freckles and cuteness galore
Verdant green eyes bringing new meaning
A symphony of creation, I must be dreaming

Sleek brown hair blazing golden in the sun
A spitting image of Venus, my heart overrun
Her smile could end a thousand year war
And the warmth lasting a thousand more 

Eloquently extending her delicate hand 
Aesthetic designs arriving on command
Producing such intricate, realistic art 
Picture or painting unable to tell apart 

Awestruck admiring her skill and splendor 
Her patience, nature, and gestures so tender
Forgetting my journey's original intent 
Discovering happiness, a place I'm content
poems.title: I thought I had witnessed Venus' perfection before, but in reality that was merely a shadow of the true beauty I beheld right beside me
notes: For Izzy. They met because the piano room was locked on a holiday.
He was waiting to take Anna in and demonstrate that he could play. Izzy was waiting for the art building, also locked.
They waited together and he read her some of his other poems. This one came shortly after.
She did not understand it. He misread the evening, held out for a proper date first, and that was the end of it.
The longest title in the collection, by a wide margin.

poems.text:
The flames slept soundly without a care in the world. Their role was fulfilled and so they kept to themselves. Unaware such a commotion would rouse them back into motion. They've sprung back to life, aiming to usurp the throne, to once again reign with their splendorous Hellish domain. 

As is my duty to life, I will bring these flames forth with all my might. 
Since these once dormant entities have been restored with vim and vigor.
And because to attempt to live without them is to willingly lack a necessary sight. 
So hand in hand, as the Angels and Demons dance, I look on, concealing a sinister snicker. 
For the truth that I’ve known has been long overthrown and of this all I must write. 

Blight, desire of an envious curse 
Coarse, promises of a lustful allure
Rancor, satisfaction of a gluttonous taste 
Haste, ruination of a slothful descent
Torment, eyes of a wrathful aim
Shame, anger of a prideful flavor
Aver, dishonesty of a greedy lie 

Falling into Hell from the gates of Heaven
Landing onto a pile of ravens’ mutilated wings
Unable to breathe from the weight of the sins
Yet despite this, he rises swiftly

Gravel crumbling underneath heavy footsteps
Ashes overhead crowning the spiteful horizon
Burning flesh of beast and man scent the land
Yet despite this, he marches undeterred 

Sun relentlessly scorning Earth for revenge 
Foliage withering into disgusting remains
Demons cackling at their affliction of agony
Yet despite this, he climbs steadily

Tumbling boulders down blocking the path
Flooding the terrain to slow down advance
Breaking the bridges to stop all progress
Yet despite this, he arrives prominently

Tarnished by vile blood and foul soot
Rending the souls of the foolish victims
Condemned to Hell for all eternity
Yet despite this, he dances elegantly 

Looking down at suffering atop the crest
Seeing heinous spawns of evil without end
Gnawing each other to disfigured shreds 
Yet despite this, he invites entreatingly 

Endless pits splitting terrain to tatters
Magma spitting forth from every crevice 
Shrieks crying for mercy rattle the air
Yet despite this, he prays calmly

Oceans receding into isolated deserts 
Buildings crumbling into abandoned ruble 
Angels gaily shaking hands with demons 
Yet despite this, he focuses pensively

Castigating the wholly innocent with hexes
Exalting the wickedly guilty with treasures
Comfort for suffering, suffering for comfort 
Yet despite this, he appreciates earnestly

In the end, all that remained was himself and his mind.
All the suffering perfectly reflected the desire he failed to deny.
The reality, the gravity, the situation is always by himself defined.
Coming to understand that of Heaven and Hell, fate he cannot defy. 
So meeting the end, he conceded to bend to the Will, but never to resign.
poems.title: Into the chasm
notes: After Nietzsche, Sisyphus, and Prometheus.
The question driving it: how can the Church be right if everyone inside it behaves badly.
54 lines. The chapter where the subject stops being women for a while.

poems.text:
Like the nostalgic return to one's hometown
I long for scenes of once familiar contentment

The softness of her hands 
The anticipation of our plans 
Painting a portrait of unthinkable colors

With a gentle caress 
In her flawless dress 
Sweeping away all the troubles of the world

Calmly calling 
Sensually stalling
Both knowing this eventually wouldn't last

With a shearing force 
Without any remorse 
Halting this tale too good to be true

The firmness in her command
The empowerment of my hand 
Driving in new meaning to a bitter feeling

As strong iron is forged by an intense flame
I steady myself with focus on her gift, Hope
poems.title: In the Past
notes: About Caler, met during Week of Welcome through a mutual friend. Named, she told him, after a billboard.
Very southern, very strange. They kissed one night and dated loosely after.
He is not certain whether the poem is about her or about Jocelyn. She reminded him of someone.

poems.text:
There was once a boy who walked alone through the night. On the same trip he'd taken many times since he was a child. He turned along the same bend and ducked under the same low branches. Crossing the rickety wooden bridge and seeing his cozy home coming into sight. A long day behind him, as he opens the door. He was greeted by a deafening sound and a blinding sight. Silence. Pitch black. Deafness. Darkness. Swallowing him whole. When usually at this time he would be wrapped in his mother's vigorous embrace, instead a cage of frost took hold of his limbs. When usually at this time he would be romping with a frabjous smile, instead a sharp frown dominated his visage. The words he uttered subsequently he would remember forever. 

The snapping of bones, the tearing of flesh 
The hate in the heart, now rekindled afresh 
The weakness within the spirit and of the skin
The willingness to surpass with devilish sin 

Bending the rules and testing their wills
God and Devil dance exciting many thrills
Constructing a tune that mortals call fate 
Destructing that noise by unrelenting hate

The pieces in place, players seeming ready 
The dice rigged in secret, the end set already
The weak making rules, restraining the strong 
The wise realizing this game feels so wrong

Powerless to change the clock set in motion
Kings abusing the throne fearing no remotion
Weakness ordained to permeate so densely
Anger, rage, and hate amplified immensely

The crest impossible to reach on your own 
The ambition too steep to topple the throne
The plentiful times trying to throw off destiny
The heart's tenacious grasp holding ineffably 

One thousand deaths he would spend to win
To rip from the gods their fate and their sin
Never bending to the cruel, twisted, and ill
For he brings forth the future by his very will 

Though time a currency and suffering a price
The fight carries on regardless the strife 
Who concedes first, the man or the god? 
Who reaches truth, the man or the fraud?
poems.title: The descent
notes: His own favourite, for the last line.
On what it feels like to stop sorting the world into good and evil, left and right, angel and devil.
To become, in his phrase, an infant among gods. The bottom being the only place from which the twilight of the idols is visible.
Also about beating his gym mentor, and watching him take it badly.

poems.text:
I see the lot. 
Perched atop the clouds 
Looking down from the air 
People covered in shrouds
People trapped by snare

I sing of their fates
I warn of their demise
For I've been in their states
And from such I've arise

Prepare your ears
To heed my rhymes
And away I'll steer
You from these crimes

Afloat the wretched sea of the putrid masses
Thoraces distended, stammering to the tune
Ruin, creeping into each of their actions
Fractions of their true selves, never realized

Walk now through the painless gate
Talk now with such fluid prate
Filling their lives with vulgar chatter
Spreading their lies with boastful smatter

Avoiding the truth that shreds their facade 
Dodging the changes to correct their fraud
Listen and hear how they all lied
Try and discern the honesty inside

Fear, weakness, anger, doubt
Coping through grasping for endless clout
Pity, sorrow, shame, despair
Wading through the motions without a care

Deficiencies in the heart and soul 
Replenished by the vapid and dull
A fruitless pursuit of the transient relief
A twisted race that concludes so brief

Replace the wasteful gluttonous urge 
With a desire to thrive and with power surge
To conquer the day, reap a wondrous prize
To cultivate hope and gather new allies

To unfetter the chains of complacency
To break free the shackles of vacancy
Challenging life with the most daring feats
Earning the trophies through many defeats

Losing is sometimes a part of the day
But quitting ought never make any headway
Full of weakness but desiring to be strong 
Pursuing the journey although it be long 

Gathering wisdom and forging a path
Willingly setting out to find the aftermath
You must take your shot, even into the dark 
You will see it causes a splendorous spark

Hold these words in heart and mind
And at once towards victory begin to find
The way that was realized for your sake 
The way, although not easy, you must take
poems.title: The lot
notes: Written from a perch above the breezeway, watching people go about their day.
After the bovine existence, and the Nicomachean Ethics.
His conclusion at the time: cookie-cutter lives, husks being filled. 53 lines of it.

poems.text:
Those cedar stained eyes 
Looking back at me 
That playful smile 
A joyous sight to see 

Sweetness glazing over her coarse words 
Levity in her tone, as jovial as the birds
Wholesome notions from her friendly jests 
A gracefulness within, her aura suggests

Though we meet just in passing 
And our time spent together so brief 
After departure feeling enchanted 
And the daily burdens overcome by relief

Curiosity waging war against my mind
Inciting action, to see what future I find
So I wrote this poem to placate that feeling
My intentions made plain by this revealing

A fleeting thought descending like a feather
What world might exist with us together
poems.title: Those cedar eyes
notes: For Sarah. They had mutual friends, overlapping schedules, and the same cafe most weeks.
He never showed it to her. She transferred.

poems.text:
Like the midnight shade cascades over fields
Shrouding Day's visage under Night's veil
The stillness seems to calm every creature 
That is except for the carrion crow 

When sleep takes root and bears dreamy fruit
The carrion crow sings with a whisper 

When joy inspires and impels one's desires 
The carrion crow reclines with a hush

Bold black wings inciting fear and chaos
But within them a sense of warmth

Grievous curses hurled at the carrion crow 
But always falling short they miss 

So distant soaring beyond vulgarity 
So magnificent dancing among the stars 

The carrion crow seeks on its mission 
To shelter a deeply fragile heart

Perched on the forking split branch 
A choice that has yet to be made 

Sharpening its talons against tough cedar
Pruning its feathers with meticulous care

How sweet the carrion crow treats itself 
How rotten an image pressed upon others 

But to the patient observer her nature true 
Sagacious bird's wisdom on wild display
poems.title: The Carrion Crow
notes: Written around Halloween, working out what a spooky poem could be.

poems.text:
Slender streams cascade the throne 
Flowing, dancing, racing through the heart
Approaching the edge of my sight, I long 

Escaping the magnetic resonant feeling 
Drawing upon stoic veils of protection 
A concoction of dissonance wells up within 

The heat of her fingertips 
The fragrance of her presence 
Fearing that I might come to hate her

Fetters granting such unbridled freedom 
Liberation, the enemy of my desire 
Shuffling the deck, wringing the neck 
Pouring out every ounce of emotion
poems.title: Silk
notes: On how new relationships hold until they don't.
He notes he was getting wiser, having now watched it happen.

poems.text:
Stirring from the void, so black and bleak
A familiar warmth, yet a feeling unique 
Just a singular glance at her tender visage 
Soothing the eyes with her flawless image 

With an affable spirit and a timid voice 
Writing you this poem as no other choice 
Wondering why in our cordial conversation
My heart interjects with pleasant palpitation

Like an excursion into a coniferous forest
I find myself lost in her eyes most purist
Chestnut brown and overpowering my gaze
Enchanting, entrancing into a dreamy daze

Like a castaway stranded on a scorching isle
Her smile provides strength to beat any trial
Renewing what previously withered and fell
Revitalizing that spirit with a magical spell

A dream of sharing these festive holidays
Without further ado and without more delays
This poem for you both honest and true 
Entrusting my heart and my words to just you
poems.title: For Mya
notes: For a woman who checked him in at the gym after he had stopped working there.
He never showed it to her, and never made a move.

poems.text:
Searing 
Slicing 
Tearing 
Dicing 
You wouldn't last a single minute in the cage 

Pain ignored through desperate desire 
Struggle endured through blazing fire
Yet for you, your outcome will be void

Fruitlessly try and try again 
Until the world meets a dead end 
But know this, your journey will be vain

Inscribing beautiful hope into the sand
Nourishing lives by the sacred hand 
How pointless! You will all crumble to dust

Slaving away the many numbered days 
Conjuring a fearsome, tormented haze
Why do so? You won't change the finale

His name is irrelevant as he lives many lives
Hungering for contest and begging for strife
Dancing on fate atop the sharpest of knives
His suffering plentiful and with meaning rife
poems.title: We Are the One
notes: On unrequited love as a standing condition rather than an event.
His framing at the time: pure of heart, and repeatedly run over.

poems.text:
Get up, now. Weakness is a waste of time, 
Stand back up, I won't count. 
Pitiful, pity creeping down your spine, 
Know this, your best will NEVER beat mine. 

Get up, here. Sit atop all of your lies. 
Drain your blood, dripping time slow. 
Savor your fear, I'll grin ear to ear, 
Sing your loudest scream, I'd love to hear. 

Ah…  
What happens… 
When I… 

Take… 
… your hopes and your dreams? 

Misappropriate… 
… your faith and your cause? 

Rip away… 
… your regard for your crimes? 

Listen…
… to your delusions when you lie? 

Veil… 
… your sanity till you die? 

Shatter down
To Hell
Your remembrance

I'll pretend to be your savior, 
To lead you out of your great misery, 
And then say, in pure malice
"GO ROT IN HELL"

I can paint you red with blood, 
When there's nowhere else to go, 
I have all the time in the world, 
Cry for mercy but I'll never get bored. 

How does it finally feel? 
Suffocating, it's your turn to pray. 
I don't need to make it short and sweet, 
Kneel till you bleed but I won't change, 

Figure it out. 
Approaching the limits of your sanity. 
Realize when there's no other way to live, 
Rotting in hell is all you have to do to win, 

Losing your senses from immolation
You'll beg to go rot in hell, 
But any request for release is met by a sinful, 
"SHUT THE FUCK UP!"

There's nowhere left for you to run. 
I might be sick of all this entertainment, 
But I had it coming, the joke's on me now. 
I should've seen the silver thread in fate.
poems.title: Rot in hell
notes: His gym mentor took third place twice at a powerlifting meet. He took second twice, beating him by about fifteen pounds.
The mentor read it as a claim to superiority. He maintains he was only curious, though he grants the point.
By his account the man's life turned downward from there. The identity had been the load-bearing thing, and it broke.
48 lines, the longest piece here. He also credits the man with teaching him most of what he knows about lifting.

image.caption: The meet. Two seconds against his mentor's two thirds. Other faces blurred.

poems.text:
Like silver thread spun down the prison wall
Leaping forth, escaping to an umbral fall 

Tumultuous waves embracing the escapee 
Potential in hand, finally breaking free 

Washed ashore, not a single soul in sight 
Until a gentle bird nearby took flight

Restoring the courage to survive the storm
Hoping that the days might finally be warm

Hesitation in accepting release from dystopia
A poem of my thoughts for you Littia
poems.title: Littia
notes: Written quickly for a match on a dating app. She thought it was cute.
She then told him she had a child. At twenty-one he knew he would not be the one to step into that, and said nothing further.
He dates his policy of not investing in strangers to this one.

poems.text:
Waking up to a dull dream
Laying still wishing for the past
Ripe fruit not as sweet as it seems
A deep regret surfacing at last

For what purpose am I contending?
For a pointless struggle, never-ending?

As I looked into my shattered reflection 
I prepare the tools for a wretched dissection 

Falling for a future in the making 
But failing to negotiate the cost
With a wavering conviction overtaking 
Happiness' sweet home slowly became lost

Emotions swirl violently down the drain
Until finally all that's left is pain 
And a dreadful aching destroys my brain 
Ceaselessly repeating this pounding refrain 

I hate you. 
I hate you. I hate you so much.

Leave me alone.

Begging for attention 
You're my sanity prevention 

I wish for such delight 
As to see you rotting in my sight

And your crocodile tear
Reminding me never to draw near

To watch you suffer from afar
Brings me a pleasure to nothing par

Hoping you will one day fall
And I stand towering above you tall

For you to realize your flaw 
And to be humbled enough to crawl 

I pray you'll never come back to me 
And if you do, please perform my lobotomy

Because I'd rather choke on air
Than be near you or your presence there 

It's not your fault I feel this way
It's an illness I would like to say
I really just need help 
And nobody seems to truly care because why would they? There's nothing in it for then to listen to a schizophrenic God complex autist. And for the kindhearted people who do care, I always treated them with skepticism because in my experience relationships have always been transactional and therefore they must have some ulterior motive. I was naive to trust the one person who gave me a chance. I thought things would finally become good, but in reality, life is not a fairy tale. Those few weeks were the happiest I have ever been in my life and nothing else even compares to the elation and joy I felt waking up each day I was deluded by thinking there was someone who wanted me. I am at my witts end and am unable to cope. Nobody will truly love me, as I am marked. Marked with autism or an ugly face or something hidden to me. There is no cope, only contending with fate. Struggling is all I can do. I am a good swimmer, but I will eventually sink in water without a life vest. I thought I had a life vest. Even only if temporarily, until I realized it was only a piece of driftwood. But the hope of the life vest is enough to keep going. Keep going, keep coping. Keep going and keep coping. Until I run out of going or I run out of coping. Inb4 "false dichotomy" . I will not consume corn syrup and I will not just be happy consuming.
poems.title: Temp
notes: Something close to a breakdown, written down.
On his expectations of women and of conventional relationships, and on being mocked for being direct about either.
39 lines. Filed under a placeholder title he never replaced.

poems.text:
Standing here 
Face to face 
Yet worlds apart

Tears welling up
Holding back the truth 
Of a future undefined 

Looking eye to eye 
I see the end 
So crystal clear 

A withered rose 
Falling sideways 
Shattering the pane 

Corrupting image 
Freeing my mind 
Let it be 

A piece of me
I see in you
So wonderfully 

Yet I speak these words
And you hear me not 
Helplessly 

A change I have yet to make 
A feeling I have yet to break 
Stealing my will to be 
Tearing at my sanity 

Why can I reach any goal
Except the one to make me whole 
Striking out every pitch you've thrown 
In this sad game that's become my home

What will it take for you to know me 
Maybe such a day will never be 
I can't let you go without great pain 
But with you too I may not remain
poems.title: Caler lol
notes: About Caler. The title says so.
He was happy, then worked out it probably could not go anywhere, and did not want to repeat the four failures before it.

poems.text:
An evening mist cascades across barren land
An orange moon hums a melancholy tune
A September pumpkin sprouts into bloom
The scarecrow weeps at his useless hands

The nightingale singing faithfully
Drowns in the crow's vast shadow
I hear it
I feel it 
But it's not to be seen, yet

A star glimmering on the horizon 
Falls to me from heaven 
I see it
I feel it
But it's not to be realized, yet

A familiar scent drifting amid the air
Reminds me of my home 
I cherish it
I feel it
But it's not to be embraced, yet

A blackened canvas against the empty night 
The intentional drop added to an endless sea
Overcome with the fear of what might not be
Staking my heart on such a meaningless fight
poems.title: Here
notes: Autumn again, and the days getting shorter.
On being honest versus protecting himself.

poems.text:
Swelling with fury, the moon waxes full 
Enthralling the stargazers with a vicious pull

A gate sealed tightly before the dead of night 
An impassable obstacle blocking all sight

How many tries might it take to unmake?
How many times to correct that mistake?

Regret.

Alas, the malady having run its course 
Vivacity dissipating with no recourse

Believing in a hope beyond the twilight 
Thinking my efforts enough to make right

Wondering what lies beyond immolation
My prayers dwindle, longing for salvation 

Tranquility I fought so hard to find
Lying dormant here inside my mind

Brought explicitly into view 
While pondering what are you
poems.title: Idk lol
notes: The same question, still unresolved.

poems.text:
Awakening from a slumber deep
Feeling so strange but so unique 

I see the sun rise and make its way 
Into the sky to begin the day 

But one also rising with a glory 
Setting out forth to write history 

A sublime pride filling the stride 
When it's you I'm walking beside

All the worries, doubts, and fear
Stand no chance when you draw near

You, my sword, shield, and heart
You, my Lord's best work of art
poems.title: Now
notes: Written while happy. Probably just after meeting Caler.

poems.text:
The feeling of mutual attraction is the highest good in life. Nothing is more central to the fundamentals of conscience feeling than is affirmation of the self by the other. The desiring of the self from the other and the desiring of the other by the self. 

The mind exists and because of this it plays a role in shaping its surroundings. But to what extent the mind can influence the physical world is determined by limits beyond the mind itself.
poems.title: On Mutual Attraction
notes: Filed as "Schizo rant lol". Retitled at his request.
Two lines. Written after an evening with Caler that stopped short and left him elated.
Short, and he kept it anyway.

poems.text:
Donning the mask 
Embracing the stage 
Enduring the task 
Eluding the sage 

Stepping out into the performer's light 
Suppressing the urge to give in to flight
The crowd cheers, anticipating the show 
The curtain retreats, lights dimming low

An empty stage, full of potential 
Starting the play, the silence torrential

Shattering the frigid stiffness of the air
A colorful display bursting with flair 

You enter the stage, exuding such delight 
You enter the stage, claiming my sight

Expressing the story with such great passion
Captivating the senses with heavenly fashion 

You danced with grace til the curtain call 
And hid your face, the veil soon to fall

But I know better than to see you for 
What you keep secret behind locked door

When everyone sees your masks in awe
The true face beyond the veil I saw 

Ushering in feelings never known before 
Inexhaustible in nature and growing more

Fleeing the stage you depart from gaze
Entrancing my heart in a stunning daze

Such a lovely spectacle you put on display 
Creating new feelings in such a vivid way
poems.title: The veil
notes: For Anna, after a Discord call. There had been e-sports drama and a long cooling-off.
On polite society, and the parts people agree to play.

poems.text:
Another hollow day passes again 
As I wonder how you've been 
I can't remember when we last talked
The feelings of regret just never depart

Now time starts ticking again
As my worries flood back in 
Only wishing for one final time
For the chance again to make you mine

Your words filling my barren mind 
Piercing my heart so sweet and kind
With empty promises all that remain 
Will I never overcome this pain?

Not too late to say goodbye 
I should have checked on you from time to time
These feelings oh so real I can't deny 
I had the chance back then I shouldn't have shied away
poems.title: Time to time
notes: Caler was moving back to Wisconsin after graduation, to raise horses.
That settled it.

poems.text:
Emerging from the lake of fire 
Demonic heart filled with ire 
Bound together by a spiteful hate 
Overwhelming with a force so great 

Pure destructive spirit free
Corrupting all the eye can see
Ripping apart what I call me 
Bringing an end to all that be 

Behold, the Prophet of Pain 
Despair at the name 
Witness his solemn refrain 

Behold, the Arbiter of Love 
Seek protection from above 
As delicate as a dove 

Behold, the Demiurge of Desire 
Enjoy the great amplifier 
Believe in his justifier

Clawing at the seams
Screaming for release 
Crushing others' dreams
Obtaining all-pervading peace 

To slash a life before its due time
To spoil the sacred banquet of saints
To trample over what you hold divine 
To relish in your unwarrented agony 

All tributes for my Dragon's feast 
All things I couldn't care for in the least
poems.title: Dragon
notes: Written with nowhere to put any of it.
What he remembers is the energy coming back afterwards.

poems.text:
The new moon hums her sweet tune 
As silver light cascades into placid waters 
Untouched by the rest of the world 
Isolated from senseless, mean vulgarities

Alone, I gaze at the pool of omneity 
Serenity taking hold of all of my senses 
I ponder my calling from the depths below
"Swim, swim, swim, to your dance with me."

And soon enough, I've caught myself adrift 
Recklessly persuaded by your innocent eyes 
Defying the laws I've guarded so devoutly
"Seek, seek, seek, find your peace in me." 

One hundred billion stars guide your touch
Never leaving room for a second judgment 
Time awaits your delicate decrees patiently 
"Go, go, go to your secret place." 

As I snap back to my substantial sense of self
With the taste of bliss lingering on my lips 
Fragments of a forgotten past flood back in
Convincing myself I despise the new moon so
poems.title: Alter Ego
notes: For Peyton, newly met at the gym.
Title borrowed from an obscure Eurobeat track of the same name.
They did end up dating.

poems.text:
Waking up with a dream in hand 
Waking up to an unimaginable land 
A blanket of warmth protecting my skin 
Ushering a new age of paradise in 

I lose my sense of self in your sincere eyes 
I see your sweet style that soothes the soul 
Beholding the world's most worthy prize 
Recognizing the becloudings of my goal

Seeking far and wide with seemingly no end
The fruit of my labor, making a new friend
poems.title: Style - With a capital S
notes: For Emma, a new friend. As direct as he was, and not interested beyond friendship.
He showed it to her partly to find out where he stood.

poems.text:
Every time I look deep into another's eyes 
Something stirs in me 
The times we shared, temporary and fleeting
Fragments of our memories 
Even though you've gone far from my side 
I can't dodge this feeling 

Even though I'm in another's loving arms
I long for your healing 
Why can't I be happy with what I've got
Appearing perfect on paper
Why now, after how long I've sought 
Failing to sate my desire

It tears at the corners of my heart
Racing from another's touch
Wondering if it will ever again start
To feel the same as it did with you 
Holding onto this worthless attachment
Chipping away at my betterment 

It might have been better if we never met
I would have far much less to regret
By none other than myself I have beset 
Leaving no choice than to try and forget
poems.title: Forget
notes: An audit of the failures so far, written while things with Peyton were unsettled.

poems.text:
The tide receding from a sandy shore
Under the moonlight night sky
Illuminates our footprints clearly
So as the time together passes by

Pausing here, face to face 
I draw upon your wondrous grace 
To make it known and for you to see 
What so freely has been given unto me

Thunder in my hand
The earth quakes by your command
Fire in my chest 
Your presence brings out my best
Liberty in stride
Your conviction strengthens my pride
Vivacity in my breath 
No longer fearing facing Death 

The stars in your eyes so brightly shining 
Frees the binds on my heart once confining
As we walk quietly through the crisp night
With everything around us feeling just right

There's nowhere else I'd rather stay
There's nothing else I'd rather say 
In other words…
poems.title: In other words
notes: Written for Peyton as a gift on a date. Title from the Sinatra song. The ending is omitted.
She had given him a Halloween desk ornament, a crow on a skull. He took it as a decent memento mori.
He is not sure she understood the poem. He wrote it after she said yes.

poems.text:
Falling falling falling
Like crimson foliage 
Forbidden love is the sweetest fruit 
Would you like a bite?

Falling falling falling
A million beautiful days go by
Vanishing into a daze 
When you draw near

Calling calling calling 
From a voice nowhere in sight 
Snapping out of trance 
Would you ignite the dynamite?

Stalling stalling stalling
The darkness on the horizon
Looming over every prayer
Blazing sorrowful tears into gold

Crawling crawling crawling 
Witness the birth of a trillion stars
From the blood you've shed 
Why would you steal such a precious thing?

Bawling bawling bawling 
Struck down with no remorse 
Wrathful blessings crown the worthy 
Embroider your heart with every frustration

Appalling appalling appalling 
Seething envy drowning out reason
Turning the blue moon to gray 
Would you like to paint my misery?
poems.title: Falling, falling, falling
notes: From a Eurobeat track he had on repeat: "Cicada Shell", KIHOW, TOHO Euro Splash.
What he took from it was how little of anything stays.

poems.text:
You were my everything 
Everything that I wished 
Everything that I missed 
It all returns to nothing 

You kissed my faceless lips
Bringing hope to a desolate heart
Bringing feelings to numbness
It all comes back to nothing

You promised my forever
Looked into my eyes
Looked into my lies
Now my world is ending 

You held my stained hands
Letting you down 
Letting you drown 
It all comes back to love

You endured my prideful pain
Spending one million years
Spending one million tears
It all returns to nothing 

I'll never love again
Till sweet death comes


"Komm susser tod"
poems.title: Nothing
notes: After the end of Evangelion.
Also after Peyton, and after Caler stopped replying.

poems.text:
Too afraid to say
The whereabouts of a calloused heart
Too timid to stay
Feeling like fate will forcefully depart


Melting 
Into a smiling lavender field 
Until every sensation yield 
Awaiting the peaceful scene 
So blissfully pristine 

Sinking
Into a weightless silver lining
A beclouding so mystifying 
Familiarity in those eyes
A part of me I deeply despise 

Drifting
Away from the me that's not me
Toward the me that I can't be 
The one held inside your hand
Surely failing to take command

Regardless,
You
Refuse all extinction 
Exist despite distinction 
Kill the urge to kill
Spite the urge to spite

The puzzle piece I left long ago
The self I abandoned to freeze in the snow 
Now shining through its enveloping glow 
Clinging onto hope, driving my spirit to grow

Peaceful as water reflecting sweet moonlight
Tranquil as doves sleeping soundly at midnight
Overwhelming clarity piercing the air
Finally realizing the answer of my prayer

Is staring right back at me 
Junsui
poems.title: Junsui
notes: For Emma, whom he was falling for by then. Genuine, in his description, and too sweet for her own good.
He glosses junsui as sweet. It more precisely means pure.

seraphim, oh what will it be, do you think its worthy of saving

taking my hand, as we once began, into the light of surveilling

poems.text:
A rose petal drifted downstream
And brought me a timeless dream.

That placates the tumultuous tide,
With just one gaze.
That breezes the stifling stillness,
With just one graze.

That rose who felt so soft and sweet,
She swiftly swept me off my feet.
And to my soul, she gently speak,
With a resonating voice, tone unique.

My rose, gently swaying so heavy a heart.
Dancing toward peace, just before we depart.
For Time unyielding, he plans to tear us apart, 
Yet our love existed, even before his start.
poems.title: Rose
notes: A crush. Probably Sophia.

poems.text:
When I looked, it wasn't there.
So I listened while She spoke.
What I dreamed, I wouldn't dare. 
So I slept until She awoke.

And opened blind eyes with truth divine.
Accepting her gifts as rightfully mine,
I’ve reconciled my right and wrong.
And see that to my other half, I belong.

Gently lowering her hands to me,
She embraced tightly, with sincerity.
Through the weary heart’s endless days,
That fleeting feeling, yet timeless stays. 

To assuage the anger, sorrow, and rage,
She tames the truculent tiger encaged.
And by gracious touch and subtle art,
She mends the wounds once torn apart.

She, the cure to all that ails.
She, the wind behind my sails.
Within her eyes, a tranquil sea,
That fills my heart, eternally.

While I gaze upon the starry sky,
Memories of her flash on by. 
Though trillions of stars shine above,
Her smile eclipses them all with love.

Let us, beneath the moonlight, dance.
And never again miss this chance.
To share the rhythm of our hearts,
Andn’t quell a love before it starts.

If more than words are needed to,
Prove the depth of my love so true,
Then take my hand, I’ll promise you,
My life, my future, my all, I do.
poems.title: Mary ( Hagia Sophia )
notes: Definitely Sophia. He was in love with her, and studying Gnosticism, and by then the two were not separable.
Hagia Sophia means Holy Wisdom. He was aware of that.

poems.text:
As the rhythm starts,
From our drumming hearts,
Time stops.

Racing towards the past,
Hours never last,
For us.

Standing beside you,
My feelings renew,
As we,

With farewell in mind,
Our hands in a bind,
Depart.

Remember time shared,
And how our fates paired,
Forever.

Far from being lost,
Or found at a cost,
Yet I know.

The sorrow I bear,
The promise I swear,
You are,

So close yet so far,
The memories are,
Always mine.

Note: Read the last line of each block.
poems.title: Mary (Hagia Sophia) 2
notes: A double poem. Read the last line of each group for the second one.
Written as his undergraduate degree ended, when he thought he would not see her again.
The choice in front of him was to escalate or to stop. He wanted to stay.

poems.text:
The promise from an Angel's lips

Though time and space us separate 
Our futures freely formed our fate 
 
The key to Heaven clearly here 
I know it true when you drawn near 

The answer to all inquiry

poems.text:
The full moon cloaked in thunderous skies,
Alone in darkness, with restless mind.
Memories of you, make my heart rise,
To my soul's perfect home, sweet and kind.

Her touch so tender, her smile so shy,
Gates of Heaven lying in her eyes.
Love on our lips, we do not deny,
That stirring feeling of butterflies.

Yet Time demands us remain apart.
So with my whole Spirit I will fight,
Through Hell to reclaim my other heart.
Never stopping until she is Wright. 

Anticipating that sacred day,
I steel myself and patiently pray.

poems.text:
Tenacious eyes,
Free the warmth wrapped in a dormant spirit.

Familiar voice,
Mends the memories of sundered worlds.

Stylish soul,
Echos the homeless heart's rhythmic dance.

Unseen moon,
Forces Fate's hidden hand into action. 

Beckoning tides,
Wash away the penumbra of uncertainty. 

Uncharted maps,
Disclose the precision of secret treasures.

Concealed semaphores,
Reveal the reality within the right direction.

Paused time,
Affords only us this momentary recognition.

poems.text:
Mi corazón está lleno y vacío, // My heart is full and empty
Tú eres demasiado y suficiente. // You are too much and enough
Mi tiempo es satisfactorio y insatisfactorio, // My time is worthwhile and worthless
Porque eres mi primera y mi final. // Because you are my first and final

Cuando la hora ha cambiado, // When the hour has changed
Cuando ha dado un giro inesperado, // When the tables have turned
Cuando ahora eres sólo recuerdo, // When you are only memory
Y ya no frente de mi. // And you are no longer near me

Aún ahora, todavía siento el zumbido, // Yet now, I still feel the thrumming
Del corazón que me diste. //  Of the heart you gave me. 
Y cuando el sonido de mi corazón se desvanezca // And when the sound of my heart fades
Espero que sientas lo mismo, // I hope you feel the same
((pero entiendo si no es tu caso.)) // ((But I understand))

She told him the grammar was bad. He agrees.

poems.text:
Two soulless pupils staring back at me,
Nothing else reflected off that vacant sea.

Drawing in an ocean of blood 
Slaughtered 

Dead eyes never again blink.
Severed throats never again shriek.

Thrown into Satan's sinister thrall,
Helpless. My hands delivered them all.

Have to kill 
So you know exactly how it feels 


Drown in a sea of blood

Destined to die beneath her corpse 


Meant to rot in a cesspit of despair 

Meant to die as a waste of air

Raised as a child ashore of hate 

Never to death be slain


Don't feel a thing 


Senses all but gone 


Can't cry from the pain 

Not the same

I may not be what I think I am 


What am I?
Stoker of the flames 


Ash coated lungs 

Brimstone stained skys 

I want to survive 

Just about to die 

Faster

poems.text:
Drinking this glass,
Reminiscing our past.

Tasting sweet cherry wine,
Wishing you’d be mine.

Burning my throat,
Savoring all we wrote.

Though these feelings fleeting,
Many mistakes worth repeating.

Emptying this cup,
Knowing the time’s up.

Regretting only one thing,
Becoming merely a fling.

Knowing the reasons why,
Our romance must die,

So let this be our final goodbye,
Lest you, too, are longing to re-try.

(Hearing them all, faint whispers call…)
(Summons I heed, a future freed…)

Seasons revolve, hurt hearts evolve.
Sun soon reclines, new moonlight shines, 

Fruit from the tree, reveal the key,  
Dare destiny, God’s mission see.

Vast visions of, Heavenly love,
Serenity, infinity.

Saturn’s blessing, fate progressing,
Unleashing thee, to capture me.

With single gaze, cast worlds ablaze.
Beyond black eyes, burning truth lies,

Her touch unknown, yet like my own.
Angelic grace, spurs my heart’s pace.

Divinely planned, within my hand, 
For right or wrong, we both belong.

To Death’s dire grips, equal eclipse,
Empty echoes, sublime shadows.
poems.title: Sublime Shadows
notes: On his prayers, on Saturn, and on chaos magic.
Also on meeting Alexis.

poems.text:
Many go their entire lives thinking, seeking, and asking. 
Subsisting solely on the fleeting fruits of their acting.

But I’ve tasted the tranquility at the heart of non-action.
As our souls danced among the stars with sweet satisfaction. 

Humbly heeding God’s gracious gift of such understanding:
“Finally, in being found, you will find your everything.”
poems.title: \[AMONG] Us  (Poem for my birthday)
notes: A birthday poem, and a deliberately funny one.
On his own inaction, which by this point he found amusing.

poems.text:
All this life is such
But to own, his each

Close enough to touch
Yet too far to ever reach

I stare at my puzzled face
While facing worlds apart

Save for a moment’s grace
Far too soon we depart

And hear these thoughts clearly
You must wear each burial mask

Desperate to hold on so dearly
Compelled to complete each task

Speaking through what’s not said 
Pay your debts before its too late

I sing my melody for the dead
To get just revenge for such hate 

To revive the fragmented spirit 
You’ve had
poems.title: Seasons
notes: On change, and on perspective. Unfinished.

poems.text:
Betwixt our fates a wonderous dance,
That stoked pure flames of fiery romance.
Side by side, we stepped to the tune,
Soaring our love long over the moon.

Tides of fortune brought upon my shore,
An angel, from God, I could not ignore.
She opened my eyes to something unknown,
Within her soft hands, my heart’d tenfold grown.

Though our hours together, seemed to last forever,
Hoping I’d never depart, this home for my heart,
Now clearly watching tears mix, with the tides receding,
In the echoes of waves, hear our song finally retreating.

```
Don’t you ever wonder why
Nothing ever seems to change.
And if it does its for the worse…
```
Haven’t you been left alone,
Such a warm heart, charred to stone.
Haven’t you been lost, then found,
Only to be tossed around.

Hold your breath, let others speak.
Why is every word so bleak?
Glad you’re here, let’s not pretend.
Why won’t this Hell ever end?

Close your eyes, but never sleep,
Promises weren’t made to keep.
Open them again, once more,
Find the same thing at your door.

Hey, don’t you know?
We’re freely forced to share this fate, and…
Hey, don’t you see?
Despite the change, we’re still the same.

That burning question of the soul,
Rampaging wild without control.
To free the shackles of such doubt,
I would gladly tear my heart out.

Well, what do you say?
Do you really want a change?
Knowing you’ll never truly change?

Well, what do you think?
Do you really want to change?
Even if things end up just the same?

Something old, now new, feels strange.
Something, it appears, has changed.
poems.title: (Can’t) Change
notes: The opening lines are lifted from Oingo Boingo's "Change".
On expectations being overturned, and on the thing that actually changed being his reading of them.
He notes he was no longer naive, or indefinitely hopeful.
The nine-month silence before this poem, and the six after it, are not an accident of the archive.

Crossing the vale —

Across the pond —

Just its choice luck —

Below clear water lies —
… A lotus’ flower spry,

With seaward sun setting, the little lotus sighed, —

> **Falling from the vine —**

> **Around it whorled,**  
> → _A round world._  
> (The cycle, the samsara, the karmic spin.)

> **Passed misty trees —**  
> → _Past mysteries._  
> (Leaving mystery behind—or passing through it.)

> **Seeing new roots,**  
> → _Seeing new routes._  
> (New paths, foundations, beginnings.)

> **Crossing the vale —**  
> → _Crossing the veil._  
> (Threshold. Between worlds. Between self and soul.)

> **It lightly soared,**  
> → _Enlightly sword._  
> (Enlightenment / sword: discernment, slicing illusion.)

> **Dueling rain for sky —**  
> → _Do you long, reign for sky?_

> **Thrown far too high,**  
> → _Throne far to high._

> **Across the pond —**  
> → _A cross uponed._  
> (Crucifixion. Burden. Symbol of death and rebirth.)

> **Or to the shore,**  
> → _Or to the sure._

> **Just its choice luck —**  
> → _Justice, choice, luck._

> **And fate’s hand nigh,**

poems.text:
I don't have a story.
I don't have a place.
I've only a memory. 
I've only her face.

A man walks intentionally through a shady grove. A September morning's mist covers his footprints, trailing behind in the soft wetland grass. Though the day is just beginning, to the man today never began. 
Nothing but a gently worn trail guides the way. The sun peaks over the soft hills in the distance, signaling the fog's time to fade. Deep in his chest, a bottomless pit starts to form. As he approaches his end to the journey that never began, the memories start to swarm. 
He stops at an unassuming tombstone, the name and dates lost to the abrasion of time. Kneeling to her, a subtle wave of grief stirs inside, but he soon forgets that feeling as it drowns in the larger sea of purposelessness. The roughness of the stone and chill of the earth ground the man, reminding him he is still present, if even only in body. Time passes, but it isn't worth counting in his reality. Lost in the past, staring down every one of his mistakes, the present choice loses all meaning. The tree resting his head resembles closely the texture of his 12 gauge’s stock. The numbness in his hands prevents the icy feeling of the cold iron trigger. With nothing to fear, nothing to be afraid of, and nothing to look for, nothing to look forward to, he wonders if today might just be the day. The note folded tidily in a leather bound journal is the only thing that keeps the man company.
notes: A bad night, written down.
